reason: Reads the installed stock catalog's provider defaults using its Bun modules. Do not ship a second model catalog in Rust.
The live extension consumes the plugin restart rules too. A native extension inventory must preserve how stock distinguishes live changes from ones that require a restart.
The app's memory endpoint filters the upstream tool list and relays requests. Move with the hub's authenticated listener, not as a separately exposed endpoint.
The app owns per-session transport and child lifetime; the external tool implementation is not OMPdesk code. Preserve the existing boundary.
The standalone app service owns its loopback listener, session streams and shutdown. Migrate both endpoint adapters with the same authentication and lifetime.
The stock extension consumes prompt and title rules synchronously; the worker also uses them to form memory records. Retain the live extension contract when moving host consumers.
The live extension and page still need the recall contract; the hub's state-file parsing must move with the memory endpoint.
Resolves and imports modules of the user's stock install for Bun callers. Native services must not duplicate or vendor those packages.
The same journal entry name and prompt-origin wire format are consumed by the stock extension and the list reader.
Privacy rules are shared with stock. Native journal or diagnostic readers must match the existing redaction before removing their Bun caller.
The worker and the page share a wire sentinel for a message without text. It is not a host service.
Stock serves the dashboard and reads messages by id; OMPdesk owns the front server, cursor, page limits and requests query. Moving the latter does not replace stock's dashboard.
Bun opens and reloads stock AuthStorage. The worker filters provider names before returning them; do not move credential contents across the boundary.
The worker grants execution to an unqueued read or a serial request and withdraws cancelled work. Move admission and withdrawal together before deleting the worker queue.
Linked and pinned plugin eligibility is OMPdesk policy. The stock upgrade calls must still honor that decision at mutation time.
Type-only contracts for inventory and changes. No runtime code to port.
Stock managers perform upgrades. OMPdesk shapes the inventory and chooses eligible changes; preserve its refusals and its restricted response fields.
Stock HistoryStorage owns composer history. The worker defaults the recent and search limits and permits these read-only requests beside the mutation queue.
Dispatch and worker lifetime can move toward the Rust lane. A Bun process must still load the installed stock methods and communicate over stdio.
Converts unsupported formats and sizes images through stock's Bun image pipeline, not a desktop image decoder.
The worker reads stock journals and derives prompt facts and completed assistant turns for the core. Separate the stock reader from the summarization rules.
Stock owns ModelsConfigSchema. The worker extracts schema literals and shapes answers without reimplementing stock validation.
Keep pi-natives grep in the installed stock worker. Its adapter maps matches and truncation to the Files panel response.

Stock owns enumeration, message loading, moves, deletion and leases. First-prompt and prompt-origin fills use stock's streaming reader. Core owns activity and typed-name titles; Bun parses only batched noncanonical timestamp strings from restored journals.
The core retains scrollback and computes each viewer's slice. Bun holds pending chunks, stream ends, long polls, PTY handles, IDs, owner checks and restart generations.
Loads the installed stock PtySession and supplies launch options. Transfers the owner's terminal rows and new output to the core in the existing reply.
Resolves worktree.base from the target project's installed stock settings and asks pi-utils for its worktree location. Do not rederive stock's naming rules.
